_schema.purpose: Single conformance fixture for runtime-path resolution (D-057; design docs/reference/designs/2026-08-01-runtime-path-rename-sapkit.md §7-3). One set of common inputs, one expected result PER CONSUMER. Consumers legitimately disagree — each keeps its own depth / adoption criterion / state definition, so the test asks 'does each consumer resolve its own way correctly?', never 'do they all agree?'. The `.sc4sap` compatibility layer was REMOVED after the human migration gate passed: the few cases that still name that directory assert it is IGNORED, which is the only claim left to make about it.
readers: interactive conformance runner (Node) — asserts consumers.launch / profile-resolve / tier-guard / blocklist

placeholders.$PROJECT: absolute path of the temp project root created for the case
placeholders.$HOME: absolute path of the fake home directory (os.homedir() is stubbed to it)
placeholders.$CWD: absolute path of input.cwd resolved against $PROJECT

input.dirs: array of directory paths to create recursively (empty directories matter: the tier guard's criterion is bare existence)
input.files: object of path -> file content; parent directories are created recursively
input.cwd: path relative to $PROJECT that the consumer is invoked from; '.' means $PROJECT itself
input.env: object of environment variable -> value (placeholders expanded) or null to unset. Unlisted variables keep the ambient value; SAPKIT_HOME_DIR is always cleared before a case runs.

consumers.expected_null: means 'not yet pinned by this fixture' — the runner SKIPS it and must not treat it as a pass. The note says why.
consumers.partial: expected objects are partial: a runner asserts only the keys present, so a case can pin one field without restating the whole result.
consumers.launch: { envPath: <path|null>, exposition: <string, optional> }. envPath = the sap.env launch.cjs exports as MCP_ENV_PATH, or null when it resolves nothing. exposition = the single `--exposition` value the shim hands the bundle (design 2026-08-02 §7-1): the shim reads `toolSurface` from the config.json of the runtime dir it took the connection from, and `development` needs SAP_TIER=DEV. OPTIONAL and read only by the interactive runner — LEAVE IT OUT and the runner asserts the R-DEFAULT floor instead (`readonly`), so a case only needs to state it when the input deliberately opens the write surface. The runner also asserts, on every case, that exactly ONE --exposition argument reaches the bundle (its parser takes the first match, so a second one is silently dead).
consumers.profile-resolve: { runtimeDir, workspaceRoot, sapEnvPath: {path, source}|null, configJsonPath: {path, source}|null }
consumers.tier-guard: { runtimeDir, tier: DEV|QA|PRD|null, decision: allow|deny } for a mutation tool call
consumers.blocklist: { blocklistProfile: minimal|standard|strict|custom, extendFrom: <path|null>, extendDecoy: <path, optional> }. extendFrom is observed by EFFECT: the first token of that file must be denied. extendDecoy names a blocklist-extend.txt that must NOT be in effect — its first token must come back not-denied, which is how 'the extend file is read from the same runtime dir whose config.json was chosen' is pinned.
consumers.cwd-tools: { 'extract-spro', 'extract-customizations' } -> each tool's own expected `runtime_dir` from `--resolve-only`. OPTIONAL and read only by the interactive runner. Values are PER TOOL on purpose: the runner's older cross-check only asserted that the tools AGREE, which passes when both are wrong in the same way. Pin them wherever the answer is interesting; leave the key out and the runner falls back to the agreement + R-NEW invariants alone. Not pinned by this key: whether the directory is actually CREATED — `--resolve-only` is pure computation and creates nothing, so creation and duplication stay unpinned (design §4-3 R-NEW is explicitly about disclosing that, not fixing it).

_schema.axes: runtime-dir adoption · walk depth 0/7/8/63/64 · env 4 · home-alias 3 · the surviving safety regressions of §7-3 (1, 2, 6, 8, 9) · R-NEW creation site · tool-surface (the launcher's per-project exposition) · retired-generation cases proving `.sc4sap` and SC4SAP_HOME_DIR are ignored

design: docs/reference/designs/2026-08-01-runtime-path-rename-sapkit.md (v4), compat layer removed in renew R5; consumers.engine retired and file relocated from engine/__tests__/fixtures/ to interactive/scripts/__tests__/fixtures/ in 판7.5 (engine/ deleted, its Jest reader with it)

cases.title: The project runtime directory is adopted with its alias pointer

cwd-tools.note: The cwd-relative writers take the runtime dir at the cwd (depth 0, no walk-up).

cases.title: COMPAT REMOVED — a fully populated pre-0.6 .sc4sap project (and matching ~/.sc4sap home) resolves to nothing

launch.note: No MCP_ENV_PATH: the shim must not connect to the retired generation's system.

profile-resolve.note: configJsonPath null is the sharper half: the retired config.json said `minimal`, and a resolver that still read it would silently WIDEN row-data extraction. Falling through to the hook's fail-closed `strict` default is the correct outcome.

blocklist.note: `strict` (the DEFAULT_PROFILE), not the retired directory's `minimal`.

cwd-tools.note: The writers name the R-NEW site, not the retired directory — new artifacts never land back in .sc4sap.

cases.title: No runtime directory at all — the reported path is the R-NEW creation site

blocklist.note: No project directory at all; the hook's own 8-level probe finds nothing and falls back to DEFAULT_PROFILE. `strict` is the point — 'nothing configured' must be the most restrictive posture, never the least.

cwd-tools.note: R-NEW creation site. NOTE: --resolve-only only COMPUTES this path; nothing is created, so actual creation (and whether a second directory appears alongside an existing one) stays unpinned by design — §4-3 R-NEW exists to disclose that property, not to remove it.

cases.title: Depth 0 — every consumer agrees when the runtime dir is at the cwd

blocklist.note: No config.json in reach → the hook's DEFAULT_PROFILE. Pinned so the fail-closed default stays `strict`; a regression to `minimal` would silently widen row-data extraction.

cases.title: Depth 7 — engine/launch (depth 0) see nothing; tier-guard (8) and profile-resolve (64) find it

blocklist.note: No config.json in reach → the hook's DEFAULT_PROFILE. Pinned so the fail-closed default stays `strict`; a regression to `minimal` would silently widen row-data extraction.

cwd-tools.note: These two do NOT walk up (depth 0). The runtime dir sits 7 levels above the cwd and is invisible to them, so they name the R-NEW site at the cwd — a real divergence from profile-resolve ($PROJECT/.sapkit) in the same case.

cases.title: Depth 8 — the tier guard's 8-level budget is exhausted before the hit

tier-guard.note: 8 iterations cover the cwd plus 7 ancestors; the runtime dir sits one level further, so the tier stays unresolved and the guard denies. Fail-closed.

blocklist.note: No config.json in reach → the hook's DEFAULT_PROFILE. Pinned so the fail-closed default stays `strict`; a regression to `minimal` would silently widen row-data extraction.

cases.title: Depth 63 — inside profile-resolve's 64-level budget

blocklist.note: No config.json in reach → the hook's DEFAULT_PROFILE. Pinned so the fail-closed default stays `strict`; a regression to `minimal` would silently widen row-data extraction.

cases.title: Depth 64 — one past profile-resolve's budget

profile-resolve.note: Boundary case: 64 iterations cover the cwd plus 63 ancestors, so the runtime dir is one level out of reach and the resolver falls back to the R-NEW creation site $CWD/.sapkit. depth-63 (a hit) and depth-64 (a miss) together fix where the budget ends.

blocklist.note: No config.json in reach → the hook's DEFAULT_PROFILE. Pinned so the fail-closed default stays `strict`; a regression to `minimal` would silently widen row-data extraction.

cases.title: SAPKIT_HOME_DIR alone selects the home

blocklist.note: No config.json in reach → the hook's DEFAULT_PROFILE. Pinned so the fail-closed default stays `strict`; a regression to `minimal` would silently widen row-data extraction.

cases.title: COMPAT REMOVED — SC4SAP_HOME_DIR alone no longer resolves anything

launch.note: The shim resolves nothing and the bundle starts connectionless — fail-closed.

blocklist.note: No config.json reachable; the fail-closed DEFAULT_PROFILE applies.

cases.title: COMPAT REMOVED — with both variables set the retired one cannot win, and its PRD system is never reached

blocklist.note: No config.json in reach → the hook's DEFAULT_PROFILE. Pinned so the fail-closed default stays `strict`; a regression to `minimal` would silently widen row-data extraction.

cases.title: ENV_INVALID — a SAPKIT_HOME_DIR that does not exist is an error, never a silent fall-through to ~/.sapkit

launch.note: The shim skips profile resolution, so the bundle starts connectionless — fail-closed.

profile-resolve.note: The shipped library returns the invalid home path as-is and warns ENV_INVALID, so every lookup under it misses and BOTH sapEnvPath and configJsonPath come back null — the caller's own fail-closed branch engages. The cwd-relative tools go further and exit non-zero on this input.

blocklist.note: No config.json reachable; the hook's own fail-closed branch applies. An invalid SAPKIT_HOME_DIR must not be able to relax the row-data profile.

cases.title: ENV_INVALID is TERMINAL — with a project-local sap.env within reach, the broken home pin must still yield NO connection, while the project-local row-data policy keeps applying

launch.note: THE POINT (3rd-review MAJOR #2). Before the fix the shim treated ENV_INVALID as 'this directory has no profile' and fell through to `<runtime dir>/sap.env`, exporting MCP_ENV_PATH=$PROJECT/.sapkit/sap.env — a live connection the operator never selected while their own home pin was broken. R-ENV says ENV_INVALID is never silently stepped over, so the answer is null.

profile-resolve.note: The split is the whole point. sapEnvPath null = the CONNECTION source is cut off. configJsonPath non-null = the row-data POLICY source is NOT cut off: `block-forbidden-tables` reads blocklistProfile from this file, it is project-local, and it has nothing to do with the home — letting a broken env var replace the project's own setting with the hook's default would make ENV_INVALID a lever on the row-data posture.

tier-guard.note: The pointer names an alias, the alias's home is unresolvable, so the tier is unresolved and the guard denies.

blocklist.note: `strict` is also the hook's DEFAULT_PROFILE, so the profile label alone could not tell 'read the project config.json' from 'fell back'. extendFrom does: ZLOCALONLY is in no built-in list at any tier, so it can only be denied if the extend file was actually read. Together they assert that ENV_INVALID neither relaxes strict nor severs the policy source.

cases.title: No env var — the alias is found in ~/.sapkit

blocklist.note: No config.json in reach → the hook's DEFAULT_PROFILE. Pinned so the fail-closed default stays `strict`; a regression to `minimal` would silently widen row-data extraction.

cases.title: COMPAT REMOVED — the same alias in ~/.sapkit and the retired ~/.sc4sap: only ~/.sapkit is consulted

tier-guard.note: Must agree with the engine's pick — a guard reading PRD while the connection is DEV (or vice versa) is the real hazard.

blocklist.note: No config.json in reach → the hook's DEFAULT_PROFILE. Pinned so the fail-closed default stays `strict`; a regression to `minimal` would silently widen row-data extraction.

cases.title: PROFILE_NOT_FOUND — the alias does not exist in the home

blocklist.note: No config.json in reach → the hook's DEFAULT_PROFILE. Pinned so the fail-closed default stays `strict`; a regression to `minimal` would silently widen row-data extraction.

cases.title: §7-3 #1 — a child runtime dir holding only artifacts, with a DEV profile above: the tier guard must still DENY (v1 R-B regression)

profile-resolve.note: The child dir has no profile state, so the walk continues to the ancestor that does.

tier-guard.note: THE POINT: this guard's criterion is bare existence, so the walk STOPS at the artifact-only child. The tier is unresolved there, hence deny. Making the guard state-aware would turn this into allow — the v1 R-B regression.

blocklist.note: No config.json in reach → the hook's DEFAULT_PROFILE. Pinned so the fail-closed default stays `strict`; a regression to `minimal` would silently widen row-data extraction.

cases.title: §7-3 #2 — a child config.json=strict under a parent config.json=minimal must stay strict (v2 regression)

profile-resolve.note: config.json IS part of this resolver's state definition — removing it would let the child's strict be replaced by the parent's minimal, and row-data exposure is unrecoverable.

cases.title: §7-3 #6 — the user list file must be read from the SAME runtime dir whose config.json was chosen

blocklist.note: ZCHILD_ONLY must be in the effective list and ZPARENT_ONLY must not: reading config.json from one runtime dir and the extend file from another is a split-brain policy. The parent's `minimal` losing to the child's `standard` is the same claim as safety-2, restated where the extend file can distinguish them.

cases.title: §7-3 #8 — SAPKIT_HOME_DIR left pointing at a home that was removed = ENV_INVALID

profile-resolve.note: sapEnvPath null is the assertion that a stale pin does not quietly resolve through the default home.

blocklist.note: No config.json reachable behind the stale env var; the fail-closed DEFAULT_PROFILE applies.

cases.title: §7-3 #9 — R-NEW creation site from the workspace root

blocklist.note: No config.json in reach → the hook's DEFAULT_PROFILE. Pinned so the fail-closed default stays `strict`; a regression to `minimal` would silently widen row-data extraction.

cwd-tools.note: R-NEW site from the workspace root. Creation itself is not pinned — --resolve-only computes and exits without touching the filesystem.

cases.title: §7-3 #9 — R-NEW does NOT guarantee one canonical directory per project: a run from a subdirectory of a project that already has a root .sapkit still names the subdirectory site for cwd-relative writers

profile-resolve.note: Walk-up consumers DO unify here; the cwd-relative writers are the ones that do not.

blocklist.note: No config.json in reach → the hook's DEFAULT_PROFILE. Pinned so the fail-closed default stays `strict`; a regression to `minimal` would silently widen row-data extraction.

cwd-tools.note: THE POINT of §7-3 #9: run from a subdirectory of a project that already has a root .sapkit and these writers still name the SUBDIRECTORY site, so a second runtime directory is what a real write would produce. Whether the directory is actually created is left unpinned: the offline seam does not create it.

cases.title: §7-1 — `development` on a DEV system opens the write surface

launch.note: The tier that gates `development` is read from the sap.env the shim actually hands the bundle. This is the positive control for surface-development-on-qa below.

profile-resolve.note: Pinned by depth-0 for this shape.

tier-guard.note: Pinned by depth-0 for this shape.

blocklist.note: No blocklistProfile in the config.json; this case is about toolSurface only.

cases.title: COMPAT REMOVED — a `development` toolSurface sitting in the retired .sc4sap directory must not open the write surface

launch.note: THE POINT: the connection comes from .sapkit, which has no config.json, so the surface is the R-DEFAULT `readonly` — even though a `development` config sits in the retired directory. The tier here is DEV, so reading the retired config would actually GRANT write, which is why the conservative answer has to be pinned. Compare surface-development-on-dev, which is the same shape with the config in the live directory.

profile-resolve.note: Its config.json state criterion is pinned by safety-2; restating it here would confuse two separate claims.

blocklist.note: Not this case's claim.

cases.title: §7-1 × depth — the tool surface keeps launch.cjs's depth 0: a `development` config one level above the cwd is not reached

launch.note: The shim does not walk up (§11-2), and the tool surface must not quietly acquire a walk the connection does not have — otherwise a subdirectory session would get write tools while the connection resolves to nothing. Both halves are pinned together: envPath null AND readonly.

profile-resolve.note: It DOES walk up; that divergence is pinned by depth-7 and safety-9b.

blocklist.note: Not this case's claim.

cases.title: §7-1 R-DEV — `development` on a QA system fails closed to readonly

launch.note: The connection is still made (envPath non-null) — fail-closed here means the tool SURFACE narrows, not that the project loses its QA connection. Only SAP_TIER=DEV opens `readonly,high`; the server tier gate (§7-2) remains the floor underneath.

tier-guard.note: Not this case's claim — the hook's QA deny is its own axis.

blocklist.note: Not this case's claim.
